body:
## Summary

Fixes the CI/CD defects behind issue #808 and moves the checks that previously
only ran on `main` into the pull-request stage, so a pull request can no longer
be green while the release it produces is broken.

Fixes #808

## Root causes found (evidence in `dev/log/issues/808/pulls/809/`)

1. **macOS codesign failure on release** — `codesign` refused the bundled Chrome
   for Testing runtime ("unsealed contents present in the root directory of an
   embedded framework"): its framework layout is not versioned. Fixed with
   `mac.signIgnore`, independently of the custom sign hook.
2. **The macOS sign hook produced no output at all** — this was unexplained, so
   the first commit added an unconditional hook-entry banner and routed the
   diagnostics to stderr. On the first pull-request packaging run that
   instrumentation answered it: `app-builder-lib`'s `isSignAllowed()` returns
   early with *"Current build is a part of pull request, code signing will be
   skipped"* whenever `GITHUB_BASE_REF` is set, so the hook is never invoked and
   the app ships without a `CodeResources` envelope. Fixed with
   `CSC_FOR_PULL_REQUEST` on the ad-hoc step only (no secrets are in play there).
3. **Auto Release blocked by a malformed self-hosting evidence trailer** — now
   validated at pull-request time by a new `evidence-check` job.

## All checks now run at the pull-request stage (issue comment 5020083365)

- Desktop + `.vsix` packaging: the full six-target matrix, macOS signing and the
  artifact smoke tests run on pull requests in **dry-run** mode — every
  publishing step (attest, release upload, `SHA256SUMS`, `finalize`) is skipped.
  Path-filtered so unrelated pull requests do not pay for six runners.
- Docker image build + `verify-formal-ai-dind` runtime contract (`push: false`,
  so it is fork-safe).
- Self-hosting evidence trailers.
- Secrets scan.
- Fresh-merge simulation against the current `main`.

## Practices adopted from the pipeline templates (R3/R5)

Compared against `link-foundation/{rust,js,python}-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`
and `hive-mind/docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`:

- `scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh` (verbatim from the js template) — a stale
  merge preview now fails the pull request instead of breaking `main`.
- `scripts/check-secrets.sh` + `.secretlintrc.json`. Scoped to the files a change
  touches: the template's `secretlint "**/*"` did not finish in 25 minutes on
  this tree, while the diff scan measures 2.6 s. Verified it actually fires — a
  planted `ghp_…` token is reported as `[GITHUB_TOKEN] found GitHub Token`.
- `.github/actions/setup-buildx-resilient` (verbatim from the rust template),
  replacing all three raw `docker/setup-buildx-action@v4` uses.
- Replaced all nine `always() && !cancelled()` guards with `!cancelled()`
  (best-practices §10): `always()` also runs the job when the run is *cancelled*,
  which is the opposite of the intent.

## Defects reported upstream (R4)

Four issues filed with reproducible examples, workarounds and code suggestions —
see §8 of the analysis for the table and for two self-corrections I made while
verifying my own earlier claims.

## Verification

- `cargo test --test unit ci_cd::` — 131 passed. The workflow-invariant tests
  were updated for the new jobs rather than around them.
- `bash scripts/check-secrets.sh`, `bash scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh` and
  `rust-script scripts/self-hosting-metric.rs --since main --until HEAD` all run
  clean locally.
- Regression test asserting the `mac.signIgnore` patterns match the browser
  runtime and not the app binary.

Issue #808. Two default-branch failures, both root-caused from the run logs
collected in dev/log/issues/808/pulls/809/.

Desktop Release (runs 29720321919, 29724500254) failed signing
Contents/Resources/browser-runtime/.../Google Chrome for Testing
Framework.framework with "unsealed contents present in the root directory of an
embedded framework". The exclusion in desktop/scripts/adhoc-sign-mac.cjs was
never in effect: 1506 browser-runtime paths were signed individually, no
"Skipped..." line appears, and no [adhoc-sign-mac] line appears even though the
step sets FORMAL_AI_MACOS_SIGN_DEBUG=1. The exclusion is now also declared as
electron-builder's build.mac.signIgnore, which MacTargetHelper.buildSignOptions()
applies whether or not the custom sign hook runs, and the hook's diagnostics
moved to stderr with one unconditional entry line so the next run answers
whether it executed. The per-file trace stays default-off.

CI/CD Pipeline (runs 29719602956, 29723467001) failed Auto Release with "no
committed Formal-AI-Evidence in 10e65ae2 records session
issue-804-claude-20260720": the referenced evidence file contains neither the
session id nor "formal-ai". The invariant was only enforced at release time, on
main, after merge. A new evidence-check job runs the same
scripts/self-hosting-metric.rs measurement over the pull request's own commits,
so the release-time gate becomes a backstop instead of the first detection point.

commits.messageBody:
…run mode

Issue #808 asks that every check gate the pull request, not just main.
desktop-release.yml only ran after a release existed, so the macOS
codesign failure ("unsealed contents present in the root directory of an
embedded framework", runs 29720321919 and 29724500254) could only ever be
discovered post-merge.

The workflow now takes a path-filtered pull_request trigger:

* resolve is skipped (no release to heal, no tag to check out); build and
  vscode admit the skipped dependency with an explicit !cancelled() and
  check out the PR head instead of the resolved tag.
* Packaging, macOS signing, the DMG smoke test and the Linux/Windows
  artifact smoke test all run unchanged across the six-target matrix.
* Only publishing is skipped: attest, release upload, .vsix upload and
  the whole finalize job.
* cancel-in-progress is enabled for pull requests only, so a superseding
  push cancels the stale matrix; release runs still never cancel
  mid-upload.

commits.messageBody:
…guards

Issue #808, second batch of pull-request gates.

The Dockerfile was only built inside auto-release / manual-release, i.e.
*after* the crate was published to crates.io, so a broken image produced a
half-finished release that could not be caught before merge (runs
29312084458 and 29485000765). scripts/verify-docker-runtime.sh, the
runtime contract the image installs as verify-formal-ai-dind, had no
caller anywhere in CI. The new docker-build job builds with
push:false/load:true -- so it also works for fork pull requests, which
have no registry credentials -- behind a GHA layer cache, then runs the
verifier in a privileged container so the inner daemon assertion is real.

Separately, nine jobs guarded on `always() && !cancelled()`. always()
makes a job run even when the run is cancelled, which is precisely what
the second half tries to forbid; per CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md section 10
the correct guard is `!cancelled()` alone. One of the nine is an inline
`if:` and had to be wrapped in ${{ }}, since a bare leading `!` is a YAML
tag indicator.

commits.messageBody:
R4 of issue #808. All five upstream defects are now filed:

* link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#100
* link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#35
* link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#106
* electron-userland/electron-builder#10027

Each carries a reproducible example, a workaround, and a concrete code
suggestion, as the brief requires.

Verifying them corrected two claims in the analysis. The js template does
NOT use `always() && !cancelled()` (measured: rust 7, js 0, python 6), so
CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md section 10 does not contradict all three
templates -- js already complies and is the reference. And the
electron-builder false positive is not caused by the custom mac.sign
hook: MacTargetHelper.js:36-41 warns on `qualifier === "-" &&
hardenedRuntime` alone and never reads config.entitlements, so it fires
for every ad-hoc hardened-runtime build.

…variants

The pull-request packaging dry run produced an unsigned .app, so the smoke
test failed with "Mounted app is missing its signed CodeResources envelope".
Root cause, from the run 29728829534 log: electron-builder's isSignAllowed()
logs "Current build is a part of pull request, code signing will be skipped"
whenever builder-util's isPullRequest() sees GITHUB_BASE_REF, so the custom
sign hook was never invoked -- which is also why its debug banner never
appeared. CSC_FOR_PULL_REQUEST=true re-enables it; the flag's documented
security concern is about secret certificates, and this step only runs when no
signing secrets are configured and signs ad-hoc with identity '-'.

Also updates the workflow-invariant tests for the jobs added for this issue and
retires the stale always() comments the guards no longer use.
